fix(apple): release downloads of closed web views

Fixes #1952.

On macOS and iOS, `Web.close` deleted the web view's handler while a `WKDownload` it delegated was still running. The download's delegate callbacks then found no web view and skipped `Web.download`, the only place that removed the `downloads` entry and released the retained `WKDownload`, so both leaked (and the handler, the download's weak delegate, went away so no callback would end it). `close` now calls `cancelDownloads`, which cancels, forgets and releases every download the closing view's handler delegates, as the Linux and Windows backends already do when a view closes.

Validation:
- `go tool nsgo test ./internal/platform/apple`: new `TestClosingWebCancelsItsDownloads` passes; 128 passed, 1 failed (`TestWebMuteSuspendsMedia`, which already fails on main on this host), 2 skipped. One earlier run reported 2 failures; the second did not recur.
- `go tool nsgo check -target macos,ios -jobs 4`: passed.
- Not run: a real download interrupted by deleting a `core.WebView` on a device or simulator.

fix(cli): own a missing ~/.coi the runs dir creates

Redmine: 54622

`ensureContainerRunsDir` (`coi run --prompt`, `coi tool spec`) ran `mkdir -p ~/.coi/runs && chown` on `runs` only, so a missing `~/.coi` was left root-owned. It now creates `~/.coi` with `session.HomeMkdirCmd` (the `homeMkdirCmd` from #1106 with an explicit owner, since the run uid comes from `ResolveCodeUID` and can differ from `container.CodeUID`). An existing `~/.coi` keeps its owner; `runs` is chowned as before.

`HomeMkdirCmd` (and so every `homeMkdirCmd` call site from #1106) now accepts a dir another exec creates at the same time instead of failing: each dir is `mkdir`ed and chowned only by the exec whose `mkdir` succeeded. Parallel first `coi tool spec` / `coi run --prompt` calls on a container without `~/.coi` no longer fail with "failed to create runs dir".

Tests:
- `TestEnsureContainerRunsDir_ChownsCreatedDirs` (fails on master: only `runs` chowned).
- `TestHomeMkdirCmd_ExplicitOwner`, `TestHomeMkdirCmd_ConcurrentCreate` (4 parallel execs, 50 rounds; fails without the concurrent-create handling).

## Performance impact

none (one exec per run as before; the command gains a shell loop over one dir).

## Testing

- `go test -short -race ./...`, gofmt, go vet, golangci-lint locally.
- Integration tests not run locally (need Incus); CI runs them.

fix(security): hash protect- device names Incus 7.6 rejects

Redmine: 53727

`pathToDeviceName` passed most characters through, so a protected path whose device name Incus rejects failed to mount; `SetupSecurityMounts` then returned early and coi only warned, leaving that path, the later protected paths, the nested-git batch and the parent pins unmounted.

Incus rules across supported versions:
- 6.x: 1-63 chars, `[/.\-:_a-zA-Z0-9]`.
- 7.0-7.5 (`IsAPIName`): at most 64 chars, start and end with a letter or digit, no white space or `$?&+"'\`*/`.
- 7.6 (lxc/incus#4230): additionally `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` only.

`pathToDeviceName` now hashes (sha256, 16 hex, like nested git paths) any name that is not 1-63 chars of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` starting and ending with a letter or digit, e.g. `node_modules/@scope/pkg`, `__pycache__`, a long path. Valid names are unchanged, so existing containers keep their device names.

## Tests
- `TestPathToDeviceName_IncusValidity`: valid names with uppercase, digits, `_` and an exactly 63-char name stay unchanged; `@`, `:`, space, non-ASCII, `+`, `~`, `[`, `__pycache__`, `build-` and a 64-char name are hashed, match the combined rule and do not collide. Fails on master; mutations of the length bound, charset and end-char checks fail it.
- `go test -short -race ./...`, gofmt, go vet, golangci-lint: pass.
- Integration tests: not run locally (need Incus); CI runs them.

## Performance impact
none (runs once per protected path at session setup).

fix: leaving a repository's tab while it is being read throws nothing

Closes #849.

Switching from a repository's tab to one that isn't a repository (the start page, Git Config, Insights, Ignore rules, People), while that repository was still being read, logged uncaught errors: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'path')`. Nothing visible broke.

**Based on `main`, not on the Smart filters stack.** The stack doesn't touch the lines this changes in `App.svelte`.

## Why it happened

The shell gave each repository view `path={session.activeTab.path}`. A component's prop is read when it's used, not when it's handed over, so a view that was waiting on the backend read `session.activeTab.path` again when its answer came. By then the tab on screen wasn't a repository, `session.activeTab` was undefined, and the read threw.

The issue named two places, `OperationBanner.refresh` and `GraphView.readTips`. The new test found a third on its first run, `Sidebar.loadMerged`, and any function that reads `path` after an `await` is another.

## The fix

One change in the shell, so it covers every view and every such function, now and later: the repository on screen is rendered through a keyed `{#each}` over a list of one path or none, where it was an `{#if}` with a `{#key}`. An each block hands its children the item they were made for, and that stays readable after the block is gone. A view being taken down gets its own path, as it always should have.

What shows, and when a view is made again, is the same as before: one view per repository path, made again when the path changes.

It reads less plainly than the if and key it replaces, so the markup says why it's there.

## Checked

- **A new browser test, `e2e/shell.spec.ts`,** mounts the whole shell (`App.svelte`) against the stubbed backend, which no test did before. It restores a session with a repository open, slows `RepoState`, `HeadCommit` and `Refs`, and leaves the tab while they're out:
  - for the start page: no uncaught error;
  - for another repository: no uncaught error, the other repository is read, and nothing is asked of a repository with no path.
  - **Before the fix the first test failed** with the issue's error, `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'path')` at `OperationBanner.refresh`, and the dev server logged the same from `Sidebar.loadMerged`. After it, both pass in Chromium and WebKit.
- **In the real app** (a separate dev instance, two repositories open): switched between the two repositories and the start page 24 times in a row without waiting, opened a tab that isn't a repository over a fresh one, went back, and closed the tab on screen. Each repository's graph showed when its tab was chosen, no repository view was left behind on the start page or under the other tab, and there was no error about a path.
  - One other console error showed, once per page load: `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'nodes')`. It isn't the app's. Its stack is all in `wails/ipc.js`, Wails's own dev script, which expects a WebView and was being opened in a plain browser to drive it.
- `npm run check` (0 errors), `npm run lint` and `npm run bundle-budget` (startup chunk 404 kB of 600 kB) pass.
- `npm test`: 1,303 of 1,304 pass. The one failure, `rowCache.test.ts` "keeps only the chunks near the view", fails on plain `main` on this machine too.
- **Every browser test, Chromium and WebKit:** 985 pass, 5 fail, and none of the five is from this change:
  - four fail on plain `main` on this machine and pass in CI: Chromium `graph-lanes.spec.ts:116`; WebKit `map-authors.spec.ts:174`, `map.spec.ts:91`, `previews.spec.ts:31`;
  - WebKit `author-card.spec.ts:29` expects to catch "Counting their commits…" inside a 400 ms window. It passed 6 of 6 on its own with this change, and fails the same way on plain `main` when its whole file runs three times over at once.
